analysis: The PR changes only docs/threat-model.yaml: one added mitigation entry near head lines 1887-1893, in what looks like the T-043 watchdog rollback mitigations. It is documentation only, with no code or control change. It says `darkbloom update --rollback` is the same journaled rollback, run under the same update lease, with the same predecessor verification (pinned designated requirement) and the same single-slot exact-version quarantine. It also says the command refuses an installed bundle that differs from the recorded release and never rolls back one Mac of a cluster pair. The base units supplied to me (TB-007, TB-009, TB-010, TB-011, TB-012, TB-013 and the start of T-041) are unchanged context, and I reviewed them for consistency. The added text does not weaken or contradict any stated trust boundary or assumption in them. I cannot confirm that the described operator-rollback code actually enforces these properties: T-043's full text and the implementing source files were not in the supplied evidence. The unchanged T-043 and its watchdog rollback authority (TB-003) are outside the supplied base units. The documentation claim is therefore unverified against code. The next pass should check that the update rollback command in the provider-swift update sources matches the claims, in particular lease acquisition, predecessor signature verification, quarantine and bundle-mismatch refusal. I found no concrete regression or new attack surface in the docs-only edit.
